name: The ৈ levels - the last sign of the alphabet the game did not teach
WHY_THIS_FILE_EXISTS: Of the alphabet's 57 teaching units the game taught 56. The one it never reached was ৈ,
the sign that writes ঐ onto a consonant - কৈ, তৈ, বৈ, সৈ. No word on any of the 253 boards
carried it, so a child could finish the whole game and never meet it.
tools/vocabulary.py holds exactly four words with ৈ in them, and no more exist in the pool:
বৈশাখ, বৈঠক, তৈরি, সৈনিক. Only বৈশাখ and বৈঠক share an akshara, so only one akshara-keyed
level is possible; তৈরি and সৈনিক each stand alone under their sign and go on `letter` levels
instead, beside another word of the same consonant.
Every level here is inside the same rules as the rest: two words or more, a ring of three to
five letters, a board within 5 by 7, and an arrangement of the ring that does not spell the
answer out. Kept in its own file so it stays clear that these three levels exist to close a
gap in the alphabet rather than because the vocabulary asked for them.
The two `letter` levels are ত-1 and স-2 rather than তৈ and সৈ because a `letter` level's id
names the consonant it claims - validate() reads the part before the dash and requires every
word to start with it. They show as ত and স in the game, numbered among that letter's other
levels, which is how ক-1 has always shown.
FLAG_NOTES: Two of the four ৈ words fail the curriculum's own test - that a picture could replace the
gloss - and are flagged rather than quietly included. They are the only ৈ words the language
offers in this pool, so the choice was these or no ৈ at all.
